materials: Preparation of Reagents for Immunofluorescence Staining of Islet Cryosections
Immunofluorescence Staining Procedure on Islet Cryosections
Use freshly-made antibody incubation buffers, and wash buffers. Steps 2.3, 2.4, 2.8, 2.10, 2.11 can be done in Kartell Staining Chambers.

Aspirate the blocking solution, add primary antibodies ( Table 1 ) diluted in 0.1% Triton-X-100 (made from 10% Triton stock)/1% BSA/1X PBS and incubate in a humidified chamber overnight at 4 °C . Table 1. Aspirate the primary antibodies and wash the sections with 1X PBS three times for 10 minutes each.
Add secondary antibodies ( Table 1 ) diluted in 0.1% Triton/1% BSA/1X PBS and incubate for 1.5 hours at room temperature in a humidified chamber.
Imaging and Analysis of Fluorescently Labeled Islet Cryosections

steps.title: Prepare 10% Triton X-100 stock
steps.instruction: Combine 3 mL Triton‑X‑100 with 27 mL 1X PBS in a 30 mL container, shake for 30 min (or until fully dissolved), then store at 4 °C for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Prepare 0.2% Triton permeabilization solution
steps.instruction: Mix 1 mL of the 10 % Triton stock with 49 mL 1X PBS to make 50 mL of 0.2 % Triton solution.

steps.title: Prepare 5% normal donkey serum buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 0.2 mL normal donkey serum (NDS) with 3.8 mL 1X PBS to obtain 4 mL of 5 % NDS blocking buffer.

steps.title: Prepare antibody buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.1 g BSA in 9.8 mL 1X PBS, then add 0.1 mL 10 % Triton stock; total volume 10 mL.

steps.title: Prepare 1:25,000 DAPI staining solution
steps.instruction: Add 2 µL DAPI stock (5 mg/mL) to 50 mL 1X PBS, yielding a 1:25 000 DAPI solution.

steps.title: Thaw and air‑dry frozen sections
steps.instruction: Allow frozen tissue sections to thaw at room temperature and air‑dry for approximately 30 minutes.

steps.title: Remove OCT by PBS washes
steps.instruction: Wash the sections with 50 mL 1X PBS three times, each wash lasting 5 minutes, to remove OCT embedding medium.

steps.title: Permeabilize sections with Triton
steps.instruction: Incubate the tissue sections in 0.2 % Triton solution for 15 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash after permeabilization
steps.instruction: Wash the sections in 50 mL 1X PBS three times, each wash lasting 3–5 minutes.

steps.title: Outline regions of interest and dry
steps.instruction: Draw circles or rectangles around the sections containing the PAP marker and let the markings dry for about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Block sections with normal donkey serum
steps.instruction: Incubate sections in 5 % normal donkey serum (prepared from 100 % stock) diluted in 1X PBS at room temperature for 90 minutes in a humidified chamber.

steps.title: Apply secondary antibody and DAPI counterstain
steps.instruction: Aspirate any residual secondary antibody, then incubate slides in the 1:25 000 DAPI/PBS solution for 10 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash post‑DAPI staining
steps.instruction: Remove DAPI solution and wash sections with 1X PBS three times, each wash lasting 15 minutes.

steps.title: Mount sections with SlowFade Gold
steps.instruction: Mount the stained sections using SlowFade Gold mounting medium.

steps.title: Scan slides on whole‑slide scanner
steps.instruction: Capture high‑resolution images of the islet sections using a ScanScope FL (Aperio/Leica) whole‑slide scanning system linked to the eSlide Manager digital repository at Vanderbilt University Medical Center.

steps.title: Analyze images with Halo tissue classifier
steps.instruction: Run the Halo™ (Indica Labs) tissue classifier algorithm on 50–100 islets per labeling experiment to quantify islet cell composition and endocrine/acinar compartments.

steps.title: Upload annotated images to IIDP‑HIPP database
steps.instruction: Within 14 business days of analysis completion, upload annotated images with metadata and analysis outputs to the IIDP‑HIPP database on the Vanderbilt server‑based platform for immediate dissemination to investigators and isolation centers.
